inputText: I think you should probably get a lawyer to weigh in here. Being able to trace the provenance of the plagiarism isn’t how you prove a copyright violation claim. It’s typically by comparing the two works and determining if they have been substantively changed and if that change is apparent to a general public. This is how Shepard Fairey got in trouble for the Hope Obama poster. He copied the composition from an existing photograph and overlaid his own style. He lost that case. Same is true for many musicians. If you copy it, even if you hide the original, the original is still protected. (Also, I imagine this is why it will be very hard for people to copyright works produced with AI.)
